title: AMD ROCm documentation - overview
text: ROCm is a platform that enables developers to deploy and run applications on AMD GPUs. It includes the HIP programming language, a collection of libraries, and tools for tuning and profiling. ROCm supports Linux operating systems and AMD Radeon and Instinct GPU hardware.

title: AMD Instinct MI300X accelerator specifications
text: The AMD Instinct MI300X accelerator is built on the CDNA 3 architecture. It has 192 GB of HBM3 memory capacity with a memory bandwidth of 5.3 TB/s. The MI300X delivers 1307 TFLOPS of FP16 matrix AI compute and 1634 TOPS of INT8 compute.

title: AMD ROCm 6.3 release notes
text: ROCm 6.3 is a release built for the Instinct MI300 series. It adds support for the AITER library, improved Triton kernel compilation, and PyTorch 2.6. The release ships support for ROCm on Ubuntu 22.04 and 24.04.

title: HIP: heterogeneous programming interface for AMD GPUs
text: HIP is a C++ runtime and programming interface for writing portable GPU kernels. Code written in HIP can run on AMD GPUs and can be ported from CUDA with minimal changes. HIP kernels are written with a runtime API, a kernel launch model and device code compiled by the HIP compiler.

title: AITER library for AMD GPU AI kernels
text: AITER is a collection of optimized AI kernels for AMD GPUs. It provides tuned implementations of GEMM, attention, normalization and MoE kernels that are integrated into PyTorch and vLLM. AITER supports FP8, FP16, BF16 and FP4 precisions on CDNA 3 and CDNA 4 hardware.

title: AMD Lemonade - local LLM inference on Ryzen AI and Radeon
text: Lemonade Server is an open source local AI runtime from AMD. It serves LLMs and embeddings on Ryzen AI NPU, Radeon GPUs and iGPUs with a simple REST API that is compatible with OpenAI client libraries. Lemonade supports models such as Llama, Qwen and DeepSeek.

title: AMD Triton language backend for ROCm
text: Triton is a Python based language and compiler for writing highly performant GPU kernels. The ROCm backend lets Triton programs run on AMD GPUs and is used by PyTorch for its inductor GPU backend. Triton kernels are compiled to AMDGPU code through the LLVM ROCm toolchain.

title: AMD Developer Cloud - GPU infrastructure for AI workloads
text: AMD Developer Cloud provides access to AMD Instinct GPUs including MI300X for training and inference. Developers can run ROCm, PyTorch and Triton workloads in managed notebooks. Credits are provided to new AMD Developer Program members.

title: AMD ROCm compatibility matrix
text: The ROCm compatibility matrix lists supported operating systems, GPU architectures and frameworks per ROCm release. ROCm 6.3 supports Ubuntu 22.04 and 24.04, RHEL 9 and the Instinct MI210, MI250X, MI300X and MI325X accelerators.

title: AMD Instinct ROCm quick start guide
text: The quick start guide installs the amdgpu driver, ROCm libraries and the ROCm Docker images. Docker is the fastest path: pull the rocm/dev-ubuntu-24.04 image and run a container with the /dev/kfd and /dev/dri devices passed through.

title: AMD Ryzen AI Software - NPU acceleration for local AI
text: AMD Ryzen AI Software enables developers to run AI models on the NPU in Ryzen AI processors. It includes an ONNX Runtime execution provider and supports LLM, VLM and Stable Diffusion workloads with a 50 TOPS NPU.

title: PyTorch on AMD ROCm - installation and usage
text: PyTorch for ROCm is distributed as wheels that target the HIP runtime. Install the ROCm wheels with pip to train and run inference on AMD GPUs. Set the environment variable PYTORCH_ROCM_ARCH to select the GPU architectures to build for.
